component.name: Matrix rain overlay
component.summary: Show Matrix-style digital rain over every screen

description.p: Press Ctrl+Shift+M and The Matrix "digital rain" cascades across every monitor while the desktop dims underneath. Escape, a click, or the same shortcut brings the desktop back.

It is a layer-shell overlay on COSMIC/Wayland, composited by the GPU through EGL/GLES2 rather than painted on the CPU, so it holds its frame rate for a few percent of one core. Everything is tunable in a plain config file that is reloaded while a show is running: speed, density, tail length, colours, font and glyph set.
There is no window and no tray icon by design. The intended trigger is a COSMIC custom shortcut bound to the command matrix-rain; the launcher entry starts the same show.

screenshot.caption: Digital rain over a 16:9 screen, rendered by the app's own painter

description.p: Dependency honesty: the package now declares pycairo and the Pango typelib as hard dependencies, because the glyph atlas is built with PangoCairo and uploaded to the GPU as a texture, so the GL path needs them too; installing without recommends used to leave an unusable install. The fallback painter imports Cairo only when it draws, so a machine with a broken GL path can still run --diagnose.

Diagnosis first: the command now answers --help, --version, --diagnose, --status and --monitor-list even on a machine where no backend can start a show, because that is exactly when someone needs to ask what is wrong. A missing Wayland session is reported in one line instead of a stack trace, and a manual page documents the modes and the exit statuses.

Adding the repository is now one file: a small configuration package installs the signing public key and the apt source entry, so a software centre listing appears without anyone editing /etc/apt by hand.
The packaging also moved to a proper source format and gained a version watcher and an installed-package test, which is what lets it be reviewed for inclusion in a distribution archive.
Discoverable and installable from a software centre: the repository now publishes the AppStream catalogue next to the package, and the icon and screenshots survive AppStream processing.
First packaged release: GPU-composited matrix rain over COSMIC/Wayland, automatic GPU selection, live-reloaded config, and a cairo fallback for compositors without a usable GL path.
